span.label: repetition priming as defined here - increased performance as a behaviour is repeated, measured in a dissected Aplysia ganglion, with no reference to memory, awareness or a subject → media priming as defined in Hoewe2020 (in this corpus), which REQUIRES that the person be unable to mentally trace the source of the influence, and is restricted to System 1
span.note: THE SAME WORD AT BOTH ENDS OF ITS POSSIBLE EXTENSION, IN ONE CORPUS. One paper applies `priming` to a preparation with no subject at all - a buccal ganglion on a dish, where the criterion is that a motor pattern becomes better articulated on repetition. Another makes the ABSENCE OF A SUBJECT'S AWARENESS the defining criterion, and proposes an operational test built entirely on asking the person what they noticed. **A definition requiring unawareness and a definition with nobody to be unaware cannot be the same definition**, yet neither paper marks the word as belonging to another field. Both are ordinary uses in their own literatures. This is not a disagreement and not an error by either: it is the extension of a term stretched past the point where one definition can cover it, which is the object this project was assembled to document. The schema has no relation type for `these records use one term at incompatible scopes`; `renamed-across-fields` is the closest and it is wrong, because the name did not change - only what it can be true of. See Q-731, and Q-632 for the missing types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition priming, in an invertebrate preparation - INCREASED PERFORMANCE AS A BEHAVIOUR IS REPEATED, and nothing else. No memory, no awareness, no subject. Set beside Hoewe2020, where the same word requires that a person be unable to trace an influence, this is the widest extension of the term in the corpus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how priming MANIFESTS here - not faster or stronger but better ARTICULATED: the first cycle of a program is neither ingestive nor egestive, and repetition makes it become one. The measured quantity is the definiteness of a pattern, not the size of a response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `prime` in the authors' own scare quotes - used for the derived case, where a program triggered from inside the CPG shows priming only because extrinsic inputs were stimulated first. They mark the word when the thing does not meet their own paradigm case
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the negative result read carefully - the authors decline the strong reading of their own null: nothing PRECLUDES priming of B63-induced programs, the modulators are simply not released when only B63 is stimulated. An absence of an effect is read as an absence of a cause, not as an impossibility
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → the chemical coding model of repetition priming developed from the radula opener circuitry (Friedman et al. 2015; Friedman and Weiss 2010)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: replicates → previous demonstrations that unprimed CBI-2- and EN-induced buccal motor programs have intermediate rather than ingestive or egestive characteristics (Dacks et al. 2012; Friedman et al. 2009; Proekt et al. 2004)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: B63 —causes→ repetition priming
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.1 — the record marks this weak — THE LOAD-BEARING NEGATIVE. Repetition alone does not prime; the priming belongs to the extrinsic inputs. The paper predicted this before testing it - `if priming is in fact the result of input activation, then we would expect the answer to be no` - which is what makes the null a result rather than a gap.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: CBI-2 —causes→ repetition priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — And the KIND of priming follows the input, not the repetition - which is the chemical coding model's whole content.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: CBI-2 —causes→ B40
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE LOCALISATION, and the reason it is convincing: the same effect is produced by stimulating the input OR by applying its peptides directly, so the route is chemical rather than synaptic.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition priming —causes→ negative biasing
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — The consequence for task switching, and it follows from persistence: B20 is left more excitable by egestive priming and is active during ingestive programs too, so the modification carries into the next behaviour.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: chemical coding —causes→ repetition priming
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — Stated as what the data SUGGEST rather than as established here - the supporting work is cited to Friedman et al. - and weighted for that. The content is that WHICH modulator is released decides which kind of priming occurs, so the identity of the input is the identity of the effect.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: B20 —causes→ negative biasing
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.75 — Hedged by the authors - `likely to be at least partially responsible` - and weighted for it. The mechanism is specific even where the claim is cautious: B20 receives input during BOTH program types, so a modification made during egestive priming is still in place when an ingestive program is triggered.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repeatedly triggering feeding motor programs from inside the central pattern generator, by stimulating interneuron B63, produced no repetition priming: B8 firing stayed low in both protraction and retraction across repetitions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repetition priming did occur when the same programs were driven through extrinsic inputs, the esophageal nerve or CBI-2, showing priming depends on which element triggers the program rather than on CPG activation per se.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Unprimed programs were mostly intermediate (neither ingestive nor egestive) whichever element triggered them: 80% for CBI-2, 75% for the esophageal nerve, and 94% for B63.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming the ingestive input CBI-2 first, then switching to B63 to trigger programs, made the B63-triggered programs ingestive with a fivefold rise in retraction-phase B8 firing that later returned to baseline, showing the priming is stored postsynaptically in the core network.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming the egestive esophageal-nerve input first likewise made subsequent B63-triggered programs egestive, with a threefold rise in protraction-phase B8 firing that recovered within 15 minutes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Bath application of the CBI-2 peptides FCAP and CP-2 reproduced the ingestive signature, raising retraction-phase B8 firing to over 250% of baseline without significantly changing protraction firing.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Bath application of the esophageal-nerve peptide SCPb reproduced the egestive signature, raising protraction-phase B8 firing to over 250% of baseline.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Ingestive priming acted by making the ingestive pattern-generating interneuron B40 more excitable, so that it was recruited into subsequent B63-triggered programs with more spikes per current pulse, shorter spike latency and a depolarized resting potential.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Egestive priming instead recruited the egestive interneuron B20, whose protraction firing frequency more than doubled after esophageal-nerve stimulation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because B20 receives excitatory drive during both ingestive and egestive programs whereas B40 receives it only during ingestive ones, the authors explain the observed asymmetry of task switching: negative biasing when switching from egestive to ingestive but positive biasing in the opposite direction.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
